framework.name: Result Area 1: Shared Prosperous Economy
framework.description:
Investing in agricultural productivity, processing and consumption of nutritious foods
Provision of support for agricultural infrastructural development
Development and implementation of Quality management systems for agricultural products
Technical and financial support for value chain clusters and MSMEs development for greater access to structured markets
Strengthen the institutional and regulatory systems for transitioning the informal economy to formality

children.name: Outcome 1: Productive agricultural drives sustainable industrialisation, improves livelihoods and ensures a hunger- and malnutrition free nation
children.description:
Initiatives were created to promote and support  the goals of raising the output and productivity of agricultural sustainable industrialization

The capacities of MOFA-WAID officers were strengthened for improved sustainable production of nutritious commodities. This lead to the advocacy of  consumption of safe and nutritious foods to reduce hunger and malnutrition

Improvement to inclusive agro-enterprises and value chain development including access to business and financial services and risk management tools

children.name: Initiatives to raise agricultural productivity reach a larger share of intended beneficiaries, expanding their access to catalytic finance and agricultural good practices
children.description: This output looks at initiatives that raise agricultural productivity reach a larger share of intended beneficiaries, expanding their access to catalytic finance and agricultural good practices.

children.name: The agricultural sector and rural communities are more resilient, with reduced exposure to financial and natural disaster risks and shocks
Government and non-State actors have greater capabilities to improve sustainable production and consumption of nutritious foods
Smallholder farmers have greater access to, and service providers are better able to extend, productive resources and services needed to improve rural wellbeing
Outcome 2: Competitive private sector generates decent jobs that increase opportunities for more inclusive economic growth
children.description: This outcome focuses on advocating competitive private sector to create decent jobs that increase opportunities for more inclusive economic growth

children.name: Responsible investment in value chain development increases
Government has stronger capability to provide a sustainable and equitable business environment and improve economic policy coherence
children.description: This outcome analysis government improved capability to provide a sustainable and equitable business environment and improve economic policy coherence

children.name: Enterprises and workers in the informal economy have greater access to transition pathways from the informal to the formal economy
children.description: This outcome looks at how much the private sector is contributing to the generation of decent jobs that increases opportunities for more inclusive economic growth.

children.name: Quality market-responsive vocational education and training is more widely accessible, improving the employability of young people and the productivity of enterprises

Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have greater access to finance and business services, and women, youth and marginalised groups, in particular, are better motivated to increase usage of these services
children.description: This outcome focuses on ensuring that Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have improved access to finance and business services, and women, youth, and marginalized group particularly are better motivated to increase usage of these services

children.name: Government institutions are better able to implement fair labour practices to promote safe and decent work for all workers

framework.name: Result Area 2: Social Investment in People
framework.description:
Strengthening Health systems to achieve universal health coverage, address public health emergencies and improve the utilization of health and nutrition services
Strengthening national capacities to increase quality HIV services and empowering key populations to demand and access those services
Strengthening education system to improve learning outcomes including life skills
Strengthening legal framework and national systems to deliver efficient, equitable and responsive social protection services

children.name: Outcome 3: Government of Ghana delivers equitable, quality and financially sustainable social services.
children.description: This outcome focuses on ensuring that the Government of Ghana delivers equitable, quality and financially sustainable social services.

children.name: Primary health care strengthened to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
Health System and capacities to address social determinants of health are strengthened
Systems improved to address Public Health Emergencies.
National & local institutions have strengthened capacity to monitor and scale up high quality HIV prevention, treatment and support services
The education system has increased capacity to deliver improved learning outcomes in primary and junior high schools.
Government has increased capacity to implement policies and scale up social protection programmes that are efficient, equitable and financially sustainable
Outcome 4: Marginalised and vulnerable populations demand and utilise social services
Vulnerable populations have increased capacity to demand & use services to improve their health and nutrition status
More adolescent girls & boys complete quality basic education and have adequate life skills
Key and marginalized populations are empowered to access quality HIV/AIDS services
Vulnerable groups are made fully aware of and have access to the social protection services available to them
children.description: In 2022, 837 women, girls, men, and boys reported and received integrated information and services on GBV/SGBV through multiple reporting and integrated support systems including the DOVVSU one stop shop, the OSC and the 4 renovated GBV shelters.  The OSC in 2022, received about 27,410 calls, provided  757 people with GBV integrated services with 301 successfully closed. Provision of GBV shelters services improved in 4 regions through UNFPA and MoGCSP support with funding from the global fund in the renovation of the shelters- The Ark Foundation Shelter– Eastern Region, Pearl Safe Haven Shelter – Greater Accra Region, Domestic Violence Shelter Home– Greater Accra Region and Gyinsung Shelter Home– Upper West Region.

framework.name: Result Area 3: Protected and Safe Environment
framework.description:
Supporting implementation of climate action, including building resilience to disaster and climate impacts.
Supporting green economy initiatives in various economic sectors.
Strengthening systems and leveraging Public and Private Investments for WASH.
Supporting environmental pollution management and mitigation of impacts.

children.name: Outcome 5: Environmental governance at national and local levels is effective, efficient and coherent
National and sub-national institutions have greater capability to implement environment- and climate-related policies in line with global conventions
The National Disaster Management Organisation has stronger national and regional capabilities for disaster management and coordination
Key sectoral policies are coherent with environmental policies and considerations to support climate-resilient inclusive economic growth
National and sub-national institutions have greater capability to mobilise financial resources, in particular from private sector and climate finance, to achieve environmental outcomes
Outcome 6: Urban & rural community resilience is increased due to access to affordable services, knowledge and tools
The general public is better informed and thus better able to change behaviour on energy, waste, water, sanitation and hygiene
Communities are better able to adapt to climate change and cope with natural hazards
Communities have greater capacities and skills to adopt environmental conservation practices, such as climate-smart agriculture
children.description: Between 2021-2022, IOM supported several trainings of returnees and potential migrants, building the knowledge of 177 individuals on environmentally sustainable livelihood strategies.

children.name: Research and private sector investment is better targeted towards green production and delivery of environmental, water and sanitation services
Cities and other human settlements have more effective mechanisms for inclusive and resilient urban development

framework.name: Result Area 4: Inclusive, Accountable Governance
framework.description:
Empowering all segments of society to exercise their rights and effectively participate in the development process
Enhancing the capacity of key public institutions to deliver their mandates in full respect of human rights and principles of transparency and accountability
Promoting access to information and services particularly for the marginalized and vulnerable groups for reasonable enjoyment of fundamental rights

children.name: Outcome 7: Transparent, accountable institutions at all levels that protect the rights of all people
children.description: This outcomes focuses on promoting transparent, accountable institutions at all levels of state and society to protect the rights of all people

children.name: Governance institutions have better tools to improve effectiveness, transparency, equitability  and gender-sensitivity in implementing policies and programmes and guaranteeing the rights of  all
children.description: This outcome focuses on ensuring that governance institutions have improved tools to enhance the effectiveness, transparency, equitability, and gender-sensitivity in implementing policies and programmes and guaranteeing the rights of all.

children.name: National and subnational mechanisms have greater capabilities to promote peace, security and social cohesion
children.description: This outcome highlights that national and subnational mechanisms have substantial capabilities to promote peace, security, and social cohesion.

children.name: National planning institutions, development authorities & statistical agencies have better capability to generate & use disaggregated data for policy, planning & SDG implementation & reporting.
children.description: This outcome focuses on ensuring that national planning institutions, development authorities and statistical agencies have better capability to generate and use disaggregated data for policy, planning, SDG implementation and reporting.

children.name: Civil society has improved capability to mobilise in demanding transparency, and accountability from public institutions, in particular in attaining the SDGs in Ghana
children.description: This outcome highlights that civil society has improved capacity to mobilize in demanding transparency, and accountability from public institutions, particularly in attaining SDGs in Ghana.

children.name: The Government is more effective in migration governance and refugee management
Accountability systems have greater capabilities and more effective measures to ensure that children are protected from violence, abuse, exploitation, neglect and injustice.

National Justice System is better able to ensure compliance with international Human Rights commitments made by Ghana to protect the rights of women & vulnerable groups, including from violence and discrimination (such as migrants, PLHIV, PLWD, & vulnerable groups identified in the UN human rights assessment).
children.description: This outcome indicates that the National Justice System is better able to ensure the compliance with the international human rights commitments made by Ghana to ensure the protection of the rights of women and vulnerable groups, including from violence and discrimination such as migrants, People Living with Disabilities (PLWD), PLHIV (People Living with HIV), and vulnerable groups identified in the UN human rights assessment.

children.name: Quality services improved by eliminating HIV-related stigma and discrimination
children.description: This output relates to the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate all forms of HIV-related Stigma and Discrimination and national HIV Programme initiatives to eliminate stigma and discrimination for people living with HIV, at risk of HIV, and affected by HIV. The output allows for the JUTA Cosponsors to include and monitor joint workplan activities on the elimination of HIV-related stigma and discrimination.
